title: Gross Profit
description: Revenue, cost of goods sold and margin per invoice line, at parity with ERPNext's Gross Profit report - trended by month and broken down by branch, item group, item, customer, sales person and transaction type, with the lines sold below cost listed out.
notes:
Mirrors ERPNext's Gross Profit report. One row per Sales Invoice Item over a rolling twenty-four months, so revenue, cost and margin aggregate correctly across any dimension the report can group by — invoice, customer, customer group, item, item group, brand, warehouse, territory, sales person, transaction type, project, cost centre and branch.

Validated against the report itself, not just read off its source. For August 2026 the report returns 9,519 stock-item rows totalling 2,532,402.25 revenue, 1,760,288.91 cost and 772,113.34 gross profit; this query filtered to item_type = 'Stock Item' returns exactly those four figures. Ticking the report's "Include Non Stock Items" gives 15,289 rows and 5,148,609.81 revenue against the same 1,760,288.91 cost, which this query also reproduces exactly with the filter cleared.

ONE DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE FROM THE REPORT'S DEFAULT, and it is the one to understand before reading any margin here. The report excludes non-stock lines unless you tick "Include Non Stock Items"; this workbook includes them and labels every row 'Stock Item' or 'Non-Stock Item' in item_type. That matters because non-stock lines carry no cost at all in this costing model - labour, packages and sublet all come through at zero COGS - so they book as 100% margin and lift the blended figure hard. In the August 2026 sample they are 51% of revenue and 0% of cost. Set the Item Type filter to 'Stock Item' to reproduce the report's default exactly; leave it clear to see total invoiced revenue. Neither reading is wrong, but a margin quoted off this dashboard is meaningless without saying which one it is.

Cost is the stock ledger's own outgoing rate for that exact invoice line, which is what makes this parity rather than an approximation. When the invoice updates stock, the rate is taken from the Stock Ledger Entries keyed to the Sales Invoice Item; when it bills against a delivery note, from the entries keyed to that Delivery Note Item; and for a return it is only taken when the order was reopened, exactly as get_item_incoming_rate_data decides. Anything else costs at zero - a stock line billed without stock update and without a delivery note link shows full revenue as profit, and that is the report's behaviour, not a gap in the query.

The report's split percentage is reproduced whole: the depreciation share first (the percentage itself, or its complement for 'After Depreciation Amount', unless the line is flagged ignore_depreciation), multiplied by the claim-customer share (the claim discount when the claim customer differs from the bill-to, its complement when they are the same).

A REPORT BEHAVIOUR REPRODUCED AS-IS, worth knowing when reading a claim or depreciation line. The split percentage scales COST but not REVENUE - postprocess_row sets revenue straight from base_net_amount while cogs_per_unit is already split-adjusted. On a part-billed insurance claim the cost is therefore cut to the billed share while the full line revenue stands, which reads as a higher margin than the line really earned. This query does the same thing, on purpose, so the two agree.

Three faithful transcriptions worth noting. Sales person is a comma-joined list per invoice, pre-aggregated from Sales Team rather than joined and grouped - identical output, but it drops the whole-query GROUP BY and is what takes the full window from about 35 seconds to about 3. bundle_qty is read with max() because the report selects it unaggregated under a GROUP BY, where MariaDB returns an arbitrary value from the group; max() is the deterministic form of the same thing and agrees with it on this data. And cancelled Stock Ledger Entries are not filtered out, because the report does not filter them either.

Field precedence follows the report exactly, including where it is inconsistent: branch and cost centre take the invoice's value first and fall back to the line's, while project takes the line's value first and falls back to the invoice's.

The window is a rolling twenty-four months from the current date, which covers all invoiced history on this site (the earliest submitted invoice is 2024-12-31) and leaves room for year-on-year comparison. Opening entries and draft or cancelled invoices are excluded, as in the report. Returns are included as negative rows and labelled 'Return' in entry_type.
